Episode 06 · Helios Station

THE GRAVITY RING

A space station that makes its own gravity by spinning. Tonight the spin is slowing down, and the floor is pushing less and less.

Circular motionCentripetal accelerationNormal forceArtificial gravityGrades 9–12
CHAPTER 1

CHAPTER 01 · THE MISSION

What happens to the floor?

Helios’s ring normally spins at 2.73 rpm, so the floor pushes on the crew about as hard as Earth’s gravity would (1.00 g). Now it has slowed to 2.10 rpm. Predict before you calculate: what happens to the push of the floor on Maya?

CHAPTER 02 · THE FORCE CLUE

Which way is inward?

Maya moves in a circle of radius 120 m around the hub. Even at a steady speed her direction keeps changing, so she is accelerating toward the hub. First, which real force gives her that acceleration?

Now measure the spin

Find the ring’s angular speed ω in radians per second, then Maya’s centripetal acceleration ac at 2.10 rpm.

Ring radius120 m
Spin rate now2.10 rpm
Normal spin rate2.73 rpm
Earth’s g9.81 m/s²
ω = 2π × (spin rate in rpm) ÷ 60 s  ·  ac = ω²r  (toward the hub)
CHAPTER 03 · YOUR PHYSICS

The floor’s push

The floor is the only thing pushing on Maya, and it supplies all of her centripetal acceleration. How hard does the floor push on her now, and what fraction of Earth’s g does that feel like?

Maya’s mass m60.0 kg
Your ac at 2.10 rpmfrom Ch 2
Earth’s g9.81 m/s²
Crew needs0.85–1.05 g
N = m ac  (Newton’s second law; the floor’s push is the net force)  ·  floor gravity geff = ac ÷ 9.81 m/s²
CHAPTER 04 · CHOOSE THE SPIN PROGRAM

Quiet, steady or rapid?

The drive is repaired and offers three spin programs for the ring (r = 120 m). The crew needs a floor gravity of at least 0.85 g and no more than 1.05 g. The drive’s safety interlock refuses any program that would go above 1.05 g. You choose the program.

Predict first

With this program, what will the crew feel?

CHAPTER 04 · THE OUTCOME

MAYA · SYSTEMS ENGINEER
CHAPTER 05 · DESIGN A NEW RING

Design the new ring

Mission control wants a new habitat ring for the science module. A smaller ring is cheaper to build, but it has to spin faster to give the same floor gravity. Above 3.00 rpm, many people feel dizzy when they turn their heads, and the ring’s structure limits the rim speed to 35.0 m/s. Choose a ring radius r and a spin rate that pass all four limits.

Floor gravity0.85–1.05 g
Spin rate at most3.00 rpm
Rim speed at most35.0 m/s
Earth’s g9.81 m/s²
ω = 2π × rpm ÷ 60  ·  ac = ω²r  ·  geff = ac ÷ 9.81  ·  rim speed v = ωr
Limits: geff ≥ 0.85 g  ·  geff ≤ 1.05 g  ·  spin rate ≤ 3.00 rpm  ·  rim speed v ≤ 35.0 m/s
1 · Smallest ring2 · Approved design
